blocks.md: This lesson follows **Endogenous Experience** in *Physical Data* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, Physical Data, § Endogenous Experience
blocks.md: In most machine learning, the dataset exists before the engineering begins. A text corpus or an image benchmark is gathered independently of the model, costs little per additional example, and does not change in response to anything the model predicts. A physical machine has no such corpus. Collecting demonstrations on the robot consumes operator time and component life; robot-free and synthetic sources avoid that robot wear but still require qualification for the target machine.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Endogenous covariate shift matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Because a physical machine's own executed actions choose its next states and observations, the learner visits a distribution its demonstrations never sampled, so more nominal demonstrations only densify the region the expert already covered.

questions.q: The section **Endogenous Experience** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A scenario table enumerates the cells the declared domain requires over low-dimensional task invariants, because a brute-force state grid is defeated by dimensionality.
Autocorrelated telemetry carries about N(1-rho)/(1+rho) independent samples, so a higher logger rate cannot populate an unvisited cell.

Because a physical machine's own executed actions choose its next states and observations, the learner visits a distribution its demonstrations never sampled, so more nominal demonstrations only densify the region the expert already covered.
Teleoperation loop latency is display plus human plus command plus mechanics time, dominated by operator reaction, and it leaves step-and-wait artifacts in the labels.
